stories.label: Massive LPG tanker targeted in Hormuz: IRGC
stories.summary: New since the 10-09 piece on the Guards' claimed strike on a gas tanker and this morning's piece on Kpler's export figures (one clause each): Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps says a mine struck a crude oil supertanker in the Strait of Hormuz on Saturday, setting off a 'massive explosion', and accuses the vessel of taking an 'unauthorised' route, which is the first time the Iran-Oman 'safe route' has been enforced with a mine rather than a missile. Lead with the IRGC's statement as a claim by a party to the war: which ship, whose flag and cargo, casualties and spill only if the pages give them, and say that no shipowner, navy or independent confirmation is in the feed. The mechanism: a declared corridor plus mines outside it turns a strait into a toll gate that Tehran controls, and insurers, not navies, decide whether tankers sail. Name the series plainly: ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz and the price of Brent crude. Who it lands on: the crew, and the Asian importers paying above $100 a barrel. The feed title and the Mehr and TASS items may describe the earlier LPG tanker strike: write the new event from the Middle East Eye update (a live-file entry, short) and The New Arab, and use Mehr and TASS, both state media, only for the IRGC's own words. Write your own headline. Dateline Dubai, or as the reports give it.

stories.label: Pope Leo condemns death penalty as Trump mulls livestreamed execution
stories.summary: New since the 10-09 piece on the planned firing-squad execution of Nidal Hasan (one clause): Pope Leo XIV, the first pope from the United States, used the World Day Against the Death Penalty on Saturday to call capital punishment 'inadmissible', as his home country weighs livestreaming an execution. Lead with his words, quoted exactly, and say whether he named the US or the Hasan case or left the link to others. The mechanism: say what Catholic teaching has held since the 2018 catechism revision and what authority a papal statement has over Catholic officials who sign death warrants (none in law), where the execution plan stands and who decides on the broadcast, and how many countries still execute, only as the pages give it. The structural point: the state that most often invokes religion in its politics is being told by the head of its largest church that a public killing is not justice. Name the 13 people Hasan killed with the same care as the man to be killed, in a clause. Write from Al Jazeera and Reuters. Dateline Vatican City; not a US dateline.

stories.label: Mamdani Squeezed From Both Sides in Week Capped by ICE Shooting
stories.summary: Federal immigration agents shot a man in the Bronx on Friday, and ICE officials are defending the shooting while blaming New York's sanctuary policies for it, leaving Mayor Zohran Mamdani pressed by Washington on one side and by his own supporters on the other. Lead with the shooting: who was shot and in what condition, what the agents say happened and what witnesses or the city say, each attributed. The mechanism: say what New York's sanctuary rules actually bar (city police and jails honouring ICE detainers without a judge's warrant), why federal agents therefore make arrests on the street rather than in a jail, who investigates a shooting by a federal officer inside the city, and what Mamdani and the Department of Homeland Security each said. The accountability point: a federal force is using a shooting by its own agents as the argument against the local law that limits it. Write from the Reuters copy on Investing.com and from Bloomberg if it fetches; the New York Post is the feed's lead link and a tabloid whose headline convicts the man: use it only for attributed neighbour accounts, repeat none of its labels, and state no criminal history that is not attributed to a court or to ICE. Write your own headline. Dateline New York. US dateline (1 of 3).

stories.label: Section 144 imposed in Rawalpindi district on threat of groups 'mobilising' to disrupt law and order
stories.summary: Rawalpindi's deputy commissioner has banned public gatherings across the district for 30 days under Section 144, citing threats to 'sensitive installations' from groups said to be mobilising. Lead with the order: what it bans, for how long and on whose authority, and which threat it cites, as Dawn gives it. The mechanism for a reader outside Pakistan: Section 144 is a colonial-era provision of the Code of Criminal Procedure that lets a district official, not a court, prohibit assemblies of four or more people; Rawalpindi holds the army's headquarters and Adiala jail, so say which groups the order has in view and what protest or march it is timed against (the feed tags Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and a chief minister; name them only as the page does). The structural point: a month-long ban on assembly in the garrison city is issued by administrative order, and it is the same tool used across the border in Delhi this week (one clause). Say what the penalty is and whether any party has said it will defy it. Dawn is the regional outlet and the only source. Dateline Rawalpindi.

stories.label: VIDEO: Sporadic shootings as thugs attack NDC supporters in Enugu
stories.summary: Armed men attacked supporters of the opposition Nigeria Democratic Congress at Enugu's airport on Saturday as they gathered to welcome the party's governorship candidate, Chinyeaka Ohaa, with gunfire heard as the crowd scattered. Lead with the attack: where, how many were hurt if the page says, and who the party blames, each attributed; 'thugs' is the report's word for men no one has identified. The mechanism: say what the police and the state government have said and whether anyone was arrested, which party governs Enugu and when the governorship vote falls, and how hired violence against opposition rallies has worked in Nigerian elections, only as far as Premium Times records it. The structural point: the 2027 campaign has not formally opened, and the opposition is already being met with guns at a federal airport. State no accusation against a named politician that the page does not attribute. Ignore the feed's 'National Democratic Congress (Ghana)' tag: this is a Nigerian party. Premium Times is the regional outlet and the only source. Write your own headline. Dateline Enugu.

stories.label: Deputados federais mais votados da direita gastam o dobro com anúncios que os da esquerda
stories.summary: The ten most-voted right-wing candidates for Brazil's Chamber of Deputies spent R$5.3 million on Meta advertising, twice the R$2.6 million spent by the ten most-voted on the left, an Agência Pública analysis of the platform's ad data finds. Lead with the two numbers and what they are. The mechanism: say where the figures come from (Meta's ad library and the electoral court's spending declarations, as the piece gives it), who the largest spenders were and which parties they belong to, what the money bought in reach, where it came from (the public electoral fund or private donors), and what Brazilian electoral law requires of paid political content online. The structural point: in the election that also sends Bolsonaro to a presidential runoff (covered earlier this week, one clause), the seats in Congress were contested on one company's ad platform, and one side bought twice as much of it. The piece is in Portuguese; quote figures exactly and give reais with a dollar equivalent only if the page does. Single investigative source reporting its own data. Dateline São Paulo, or Brasília if the report files from there.

stories.label: Mexican judge sentences three men for murders of Australian, US surfers
stories.summary: A judge in Baja California has found three men guilty of murdering two Australian brothers and their American friend, killed in April 2024 on a surfing trip near Ensenada, closing a trial that ended on Friday. Lead with the verdict and the sentences as Al Jazeera gives them, and name the three dead. The mechanism: say what the court found happened (a robbery of their vehicle, as prosecutors argued), what evidence carried the case and how long it took to reach a verdict. The structural point, and the reason this is more than a crime report: the great majority of homicides in Mexico never reach a conviction, and this one did within two and a half years because the victims were foreigners and two governments were watching; say so only with a figure the page or its sources supply, and say what Mexican families of the disappeared in the same state have said if the report records it. Single source. Dateline Ensenada, or Tijuana if the court sat there.

stories.label: Infosys sees no material impact from U.S. PERM suspension
stories.summary: The US government has suspended Infosys from the Permanent Labor Certification (PERM) programme, the route by which an employer sponsors a skilled foreign worker for a green card, and India's second-largest IT exporter says it expects no material impact. Lead with the suspension, not the company's reassurance: who ordered it, on what grounds and for how long, as the report gives it, and whether TCS, Wipro or HCLTech (all tagged) are covered too. The mechanism: say what PERM is and how it differs from the H-1B visa (one lets a worker in for years, the other lets them stay), how many Infosys staff in the US have applications pending if the page says, and why the firm can call it immaterial: its revenue depends on billing workers, not on their residency. Who it lands on: the Indian engineers whose path to permanent residence stops while their employer's earnings do not. The structural point: Washington is tightening skilled migration firm by firm, and India's largest services export runs through it. The page is Investing.com copy on Yahoo with a stock-tip insert: ignore the insert and give no share-price recap. Single source. Dateline Bengaluru, where Infosys is based and where it lands; not a US dateline.

stories.label: 收废品，怎么就成了大生意？
stories.summary: TMTPost, a mainland Chinese business outlet, reports on how scrap collection in China became a large industry whose prices are set far from the scrapyard: the scale at a local depot, it writes, is tied to the commodity markets of London, New York and Brussels. Lead with the most concrete figure the piece gives for the size of the trade or of one company in it. The mechanism: say how a price on the London Metal Exchange reaches a neighbourhood collector (which metals, through which tiers of dealers and smelters), what has drawn capital into the business (metal prices, Beijing's recycling and 'circular economy' targets, the European Union's rules on scrap and carbon, as the piece gives them), and who captures the margin. Who it lands on: the informal collectors at the bottom of the chain, if the piece reports on them. If the piece centres on copper, name the series plainly as the price of copper; do not name it otherwise. This is a business feature in Chinese, not a wire report: translate figures exactly, attribute analysis to the outlet, and keep to what it documents. Single source. Dateline Beijing, or the city the report is filed from.

stories.label: Why Ketamine Immobilizes Some Users
stories.summary: Researchers have worked out why ketamine can leave some people nearly catatonic, awake but unable to move, an effect that strikes hardest in those taking a potent dose for the first time, the New York Times reports. Lead with the finding as the researchers state it. The mechanism for a technical reader: say what the study measured and in whom (people, animals, or cells; the URL points to Cornell and to anaesthesia research), which receptor or brain circuit the immobility is traced to and how that differs from the drug's anaesthetic and antidepressant actions, and how dose and prior exposure change the result. Why it matters: ketamine is now prescribed for depression in clinics and sold on the street at unknown strengths, and a user who cannot move cannot call for help. Name the journal, the lead author and the institution if the page does, and state the limits: sample size, and whether the result has been shown in humans. Single source, and the page may be paywalled past its opening: write only what is readable. Dateline New York, or Ithaca, as the report places the lead institution. US dateline (2 of 3).

stories.label: As AI mass-produces historical dramas in China, where are the boundaries?
stories.summary: AI video generation has made the Chinese historical drama, once the most expensive genre to shoot, something a small team or one person can produce, and TechNode asks where regulators and platforms will draw the line. Lead with the scale: how many AI-made historical titles or how much cheaper a production has become, in the page's own numbers. The mechanism for a technical reader: say which generation and compositing tools are used and from which companies, what a production pipeline now looks like against a studio shoot, and where the output is distributed (the short-drama apps). Then the boundary the headline asks about: what Chinese regulators have said or done about AI-generated depictions of history, a subject the state polices closely, what the platforms require in labelling, and what actors and crews lose. The structural point: the first country to industrialise AI video for mass entertainment is also the one with the firmest official view of its own history. TechNode is a Chinese tech outlet; attribute judgements to it and to the people it quotes. Single source. Dateline Beijing, or the city the report is filed from.

stories.label: XPENG names robotaxi service YOYO and opens invitation-based registration in China
stories.summary: The Chinese carmaker XPENG has branded its robotaxi business XPENG YOYO and, on 8 October, opened registration to the public in China by invitation code, moving beyond tests limited to its own employees. Lead with the opening and what it is: a staged, invitation-only step, not a commercial launch. The mechanism for a technical reader: the car runs on four of XPENG's own Turing AI chips with a combined 3,000 TOPS of computing power; say what sensors it uses and whether it relies on lidar and high-definition maps, in which cities it operates and whether a safety driver is aboard, what permit it holds, and how it compares with Baidu's Apollo Go, Pony.ai and Tesla, only as the page gives it. The structural point: a carmaker designing its own inference chips for a driverless fleet shows how far China's auto industry has moved from US silicon under export controls. Performance figures are the company's: attribute them. Single source. Dateline Guangzhou, where XPENG is based, unless the report places it elsewhere.

stories.label: Agentic开发时代到来！鸿蒙PC三大原生开发工具公测，补齐国产操作系统生态关键短板
stories.summary: Huawei opened three developer tools to public beta on HarmonyOS PCs on 8 October: the DevEco Studio IDE, an AI coding agent called DevEco Code, and DevEco CLI, a command-line kit that exposes the HarmonyOS toolchain and more than 70 'skills' to outside AI agents. Lead with what this changes: until now HarmonyOS apps were built on Windows or macOS machines, and the system can now be developed on itself. The mechanism for a developer: say what each tool does, how DevEco Code's plan-then-build and goal modes keep a human approving changes, that the CLI is built so third-party coding agents can drive HarmonyOS builds, and that phone and tablet builds run on the PC without an emulator. The number that matters: Huawei says devices on HarmonyOS 6 and 7 have passed 90 million. The structural point: an operating system cut off from Google and Microsoft by US sanctions lives or dies on whether developers write for it, and Huawei is betting that AI agents lower that cost. Zhidx is a mainland Chinese tech outlet and the piece reads close to Huawei's own announcement: attribute every claim to Huawei or the outlet, drop the promotional language, and say which model powers DevEco Code only if the page does. In Chinese. Single source. Write your own headline. Dateline Shenzhen.

stories.label: 编程体验接近Opus 5.5？谷歌Gemini 4新版本曝光
stories.summary: Google is testing a new version of Gemini 4 internally, code-named Carbon, on its in-house coding platform Jetski, and some employees say its coding feels comparable to Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5, Business Insider reported, as relayed by the Chinese outlet Zhidx. Lead with what is known and its weight: employee impressions from internal channels, with one of them adding that more testing is needed, and Google declining to comment. The mechanism for a technical reader: Gemini 4 Argon was announced on 1 October for software engineering, enterprise work and cyber defence and is not yet public; internal documents show several variants (Argon, Barium, Carbon) whose code names do not map to release names, and an early Argon build was judged closer to the older Opus 5; it is unclear whether Carbon ships as an Argon update or a separate model. The structural point: coding is where the frontier labs now compete for developers, and Google is measured, by its own staff, against a rival's model. This is a leak, not a benchmark: state no capability as fact, give no scores, and attribute every judgement to the unnamed employees via Business Insider. Zhidx is a translation of that report, in Chinese; say so. Single source. Dateline Mountain View. US dateline (3 of 3).

stories.label: Riyadh airport suspends operations leaves several wounded
stories.summary: New since the 10-09 piece on airlines halting Riyadh flights (one clause): a Houthi ballistic missile has now hit a passenger terminal, Terminal 3 of King Khalid International Airport, wounding travellers, and the airport itself was evacuated and suspended operations, where before it was carriers that chose to stop. Lead with the wounded, counted as the authority that gave each figure counted them (Saudi officials, health sources, the Houthis), and say what is not confirmed. The mechanism: say what the Houthis claim they were answering (the Saudi-led air campaign and this week's government offensive around Bab el-Mandeb, covered 10-10, one clause), what Saudi air defences did, how long the airport was shut and which flights were diverted, and what a closed capital airport means for a kingdom already cut off by sea on two sides. Count the dead and wounded in Yemen and in Saudi Arabia with the same care, each attributed. Write from the BBC, The New Arab (the regional outlet in the cluster) and the agency copy on News18; the Haberler page is a short Turkish aggregator item, used only where the others agree. Write your own headline. Dateline Riyadh.

stories.label: Trump says Ukraine should elect a new president
stories.summary: Donald Trump has said Ukraine should 'get a new president', arguing Volodymyr Zelenskyy has repeatedly failed to reach a deal with Russia. New since the 10-10 piece on the Miami talks and the 10-09 piece on the Trump-Putin diesel accord (one clause each): the host of the peace talks is now calling for the removal of one party's elected leader, a day after Zelenskyy called the diesel purchase 'an investment in a war'. Lead with Trump's words, quoted exactly and attributed, and where he said them. The mechanism: Ukraine is under martial law, which bars elections, so say what holding a vote would require and who has demanded one before (Moscow has long called Zelenskyy illegitimate), what Kyiv and the European governments replied, and what leverage Washington holds over Kyiv: intelligence, Starlink, arms deliveries, only as the reports give it. Who it lands on: Ukrainians whose territory is being negotiated by a mediator that has taken a side on who governs them. A statement is not a policy: say whether any aid or talks were made conditional on it. Write from Deutsche Welle and Ukrainska Pravda; TRT World is Turkish state media and is used where it agrees. Dateline Washington, or wherever the reports place the remarks. US dateline (1 of 3).

stories.label: Putin relays Iran's terms for ending war to Trump
stories.summary: The Kremlin said on Saturday that Vladimir Putin conveyed Iran's position on a possible agreement to end the war to Donald Trump during their phone call on Friday, Iran's state-run Mehr news agency reported. New since the 10-09 pieces on Putin's offer to Pezeshkian in Turkmenistan and on the diesel accord from the same call (one clause each): the offer to mediate has become an act, and the call that produced a fuel deal also carried Tehran's terms. Lead with the Kremlin's statement, as a statement. The mechanism: say what terms were relayed, only if the page gives them, what Washington has said in reply, how this channel sits beside the direct US-Iran talks Pezeshkian confirmed, and what Moscow gains by being the go-between for a war that keeps oil above $100 while it sells diesel to the US. Who it lands on: Iranians under bombardment and sanctions, and everyone downstream of the Strait of Hormuz. Mehr is Iranian state media and the only source in the feed, reporting a Kremlin announcement: attribute every sentence, state no term or concession as fact, and say no US confirmation is in the feed. Mehr is also the regional outlet. Dateline Moscow.

stories.label: Thousands join major pro-Palestine march in London
stories.summary: Thousands marched through central London and through Edinburgh to the Scottish Parliament on Saturday, three years after the start of the war in Gaza. Lead with the two marches and the anniversary: who organised them (the Palestine Coalition in London), how many came, each figure attributed to police or organisers, and what they demanded of the British and Scottish governments. The mechanism: say what conditions the Metropolitan Police imposed on the London route and under which law, whether there were arrests and for what, and what the UK's current position on arms exports to Israel and on recognition is, only as the pages give it. The structural point: three years on, the protest is still weekly-scale and the state's response has shifted from policing crowds to restricting them. Give the Gaza death toll only if a page carries it, attributed to the health ministry. Write the Edinburgh half from the BBC, which is independent and lifts the state-media label; Mehr is Iranian state media relaying 'local UK media' on London, so attribute what comes from it. Write your own headline. Dateline London.

stories.label: Exasperation and Resignation in Greece Over Allegations Against Kimberly Guilfoyle
stories.summary: Greeks are reacting to revelations this week about Kimberly Guilfoyle, the US ambassador in Athens, after a Republican donor's account of her conduct was reported (the Wall Street Journal and an American Express card are tagged; state the allegation exactly as the New York Times does and no further). Lead with the allegation and who made it, as an allegation, then how Athens has answered: what the Greek government, opposition and press have said, and why the piece calls the mood resignation. The mechanism: an ambassadorship given to a political ally and former partner of the president's son was confirmed by the Senate, so say what vetting that involved, what the State Department and Guilfoyle have replied, and whether any inquiry has been opened. The structural point for the reader: a small ally that hosts US bases and depends on Washington against Turkey has little room to object to who is sent to it. She has been charged with nothing unless the report says otherwise; leave out the party and Vogue colour beyond a clause. Single source, and the page may be paywalled past its opening: write only what is readable. Dateline Athens, which is where it lands; not a US dateline.

stories.label: SEC warns Nigerians against investing with unregistered WayvePay
stories.summary: Nigeria's Securities and Exchange Commission has warned the public against WayvePay, an online investment platform it says is not registered to operate in the capital market. Lead with the warning and what the platform offers, as the regulator describes it: the returns promised, how deposits are taken, and how many users it claims if the page says. The mechanism: say what registration requires and what powers the SEC has against an unregistered operator under the Investments and Securities Act (a warning freezes nothing unless the page says it did), whether WayvePay has replied, and the pattern this sits in, only as Premium Times records it: unregistered schemes that took Nigerians' savings before collapsing, in an economy where inflation outruns bank deposit rates and pushes savers toward anything that promises more. Who it lands on: small savers with no deposit insurance on such platforms. A warning is not a finding of fraud: state no allegation the SEC did not make. This is about a regulator's action, not the naira. Ignore the feed's 'U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission' tag: it is Nigeria's SEC. Premium Times is the regional outlet and the only source. Dateline Abuja.

stories.label: Russian forces strike Kiev data center used by Ukrainian army to store intelligence
stories.summary: Russia's Defence Ministry says its forces struck an Ukrsibbank data centre in Kyiv that it claims the Ukrainian military used to store intelligence, Russian state news agency TASS reported. Lead with the claim as a claim, and with the answer it is: two days after Ukrainian drones disabled a second Yandex data centre in Russia (covered 10-09, one clause), Moscow says it has hit one in the Ukrainian capital, so data centres are now being traded as targets by both sides. The mechanism for a technical reader: say what the ministry says was hit and with what, that Ukrsibbank is a commercial bank (owned by France's BNP Paribas; say so only if the page does) so the military-use claim is the legal justification Moscow is offering for striking civilian infrastructure, and what is not known: damage, casualties, whether banking services went down. The same statement claims a strike on a cargo ship carrying military supplies to Odesa: one sentence, attributed. TASS is state media and the only source, so attribute every sentence, state nothing as fact, and say that no Ukrainian or independent confirmation is in the feed. Use 'Kyiv', not the feed title's spelling, and write your own headline. Dateline Kyiv.

stories.label: Yemen govt say advancing against Houthis around Bab al-Mandeb
stories.summary: Yemen's Saudi-backed government says its forces are advancing on Houthi positions around the Bab al-Mandeb strait but have not secured the waterway, military sources told AFP, a week after it announced an operation to retake lost territory; a Saudi envoy has gone further and claimed the Houthis have lost the strait, which Al-Monitor examines. Lead with the gap between the two claims: what the military sources say is held and what is not (Perim island is tagged), each attributed, with casualty figures only if the pages give them. The mechanism: say what the Houthis seized at the mouth of the Red Sea since February and why it matters, who is fighting for the government and with what air support, and what Riyadh gains by declaring the strait reopened before it is. Name the series plainly: ship traffic through Bab el-Mandeb. Who it lands on: Yemenis in the coastal districts being fought over, and the importers whose cargo has been routed around Africa. New since the 10-09 pieces on the Red Sea escalation and the Houthi strikes on Riyadh (one clause each). Every territorial claim is a claim by a party to the war: no independent verification is in the feed, so say so. The New Arab is the regional outlet. Dateline Aden, or as the AFP copy gives it.

stories.label: Abhijeet Dipke's family unsure if he can attend grandmother's last rites after detention
stories.summary: New since this morning's piece on the detention of three former chief ministers (one clause): Delhi police have now detained Abhijeet Dipke, the founder of the Cockroach Janta Party whose rally against the Chief Election Commissioner the capital was locked down to stop, his party says it cannot reach him and calls the detention an 'abduction', and the Delhi Metro has extended the closure of 45 stations from 6 pm to 10 pm, a day after the Supreme Court told the government it could not stop trains into the city. Lead with the founder's detention: where he was taken (the airport is tagged), on what legal basis, and what the police say, each attributed. Then the closure extension, from https://www.cnbctv18.com/india/delhi-metro-extends-closure-of-45-stations-till-10-pm-amid-protest-20009143.htm . The mechanism: the state has removed the organiser as well as the opposition leaders, and kept the transport shutdown the court questioned; say where the contempt petition stands if the pages do. The grandmother's death is one sentence of human detail, not the story. Say whether anyone detained today has been released. Detention figures only as attributed. Both sources are Indian; write your own headline. Dateline New Delhi.

stories.label: Flydubai co-pilot began radicalisation in Australia, UAE prosecutors say
stories.summary: New since the 10-09 piece on the prosecutors' 'suicide mission' finding (one clause): the Emirati attorney general has now named the co-pilot, Hammam al-Hammami, and says his turn towards extremism began while he was a student in Melbourne, which moves part of the case to Australia. Lead with that statement as an accusation by a state that has not yet tested it in court. The mechanism: say what evidence the prosecutors cite for the radicalisation and for the two earlier flights to Tel Aviv, what charges he faces and when a trial is expected, and what Australian authorities have said in reply, only as the Guardian reports it. The accountability point: a pilot passed the screening of two countries and an airline, and the UAE's account places the origin of the failure abroad; say what flydubai and the aviation regulator have said about vetting. State nothing about his nationality or beliefs beyond what is attributed. Write from the Guardian; WION and the Mirror only where they agree. No Gulf or regional outlet in this cycle's feed carried it. Dateline Abu Dhabi, or Dubai as the report gives it.

stories.label: 10 terrorists killed during CTD operation in Barkhan, says Balochistan govt
stories.summary: Balochistan's Home Department says its Counter-Terrorism Department killed ten armed men in an intelligence-based operation in Barkhan district. Lead with the ten dead and who says so: the only account is the provincial government's, so 'terrorists' is its word, attributed, and the article says plainly that no independent confirmation of who the dead were is available. The mechanism: say which group the department says they belonged to and what it says was recovered, whether any officers were hurt, and whether the dead have been named or handed to families, each only as Dawn gives it. The structural point for the reader: Pakistan's largest and poorest province is fought over in operations whose only record is an official statement, in a province where families have long protested enforced disappearances and staged encounters; raise that only as far as the report does, and give the count of recent operations if it has one. Ignore the feed's 'India', 'Home Office' and 'CTD (instrument)' tags unless the page itself names India. Dawn is the regional outlet and the only source. Dateline Quetta.

stories.label: Bitcoin, ether liquidity rebounds a year after $19 billion crypto crash
stories.summary: A year to the day after the largest liquidation in crypto history wiped out $19 billion of leveraged positions, bitcoin and ether order books hold more resting liquidity than before the crash, while weekly spot volume is down nearly two-thirds from the crash week and smaller tokens have not recovered, CoinDesk reports. Lead with that split, in the page's own numbers. The mechanism for a technical reader: say what order-book depth measures and why it, not volume, decides how far a price falls when positions are force-sold; what set off the 10 October 2025 cascade (the page ties it to a Trump tariff announcement) and how exchange liquidation engines turned it into a rout; and what has and has not changed in market structure since. Who it lands on: holders of the thinly traded tokens, where the same sell order still moves the price many times further. Name the series plainly: bitcoin. Distinct from this morning's piece on bitcoin's volatility statistics (one clause at most). This is analysis of market data: no price target, and every figure attributed to the data provider the page names. Single specialist source. Give the article a dateline and location: New York, unless the report files from elsewhere.

stories.label: The psychedelic brain looks like chaos -- underneath, there's order
stories.summary: For a decade the accepted picture has been that psychedelics dissolve the brain's stable networks into noise; a new study reported by Ars Technica finds structure underneath the apparent chaos. Lead with the finding as the researchers state it, and what it overturns. The mechanism for a technical reader: say which drug and dose were studied (psilocybin is tagged) and in how many people or animals, what was measured (EEG, fMRI, as the page gives it) and what analysis revealed the order that the usual entropy measures miss, and how the result differs from the 'entropic brain' account. Why it matters: psilocybin is in late-stage trials for depression, and what the drug does to brain networks is the stated rationale for the therapy. Name the journal, lead author and institution if the page does, and state the limits: sample size, and that a pattern in brain recordings is not yet a clinical result. Single specialist source. Give the article a dateline and location: the city of the lead institution as the report gives it.

stories.label: Scientists Detect Record-Breaking Radio Signal from the Ancient Universe
stories.summary: A fast radio burst detected in 2024 travelled about 10 billion light years to reach Earth, doubling the distance record for these millisecond-long, still unexplained flashes, 404 Media reports. Lead with the distance and the doubling. The mechanism for a technical reader: say which telescope caught the burst and how its distance was established (the host galaxy's redshift, and the dispersion of the signal by the electrons it crossed, as the page gives it), how much energy it must have released to be seen from that far, and why a burst this distant is useful: its dispersion weighs the ordinary matter spread thinly between galaxies across most of cosmic history. Say what the result does and does not settle about what produces the bursts (magnetars are the leading candidate only if the piece says so). Name the journal, the lead author and the institution if the page does. The feed entry was a short summary: write only what the page supports. Single specialist source. Give the article a dateline and location: the observatory or the city of the lead institution as the report gives it.

stories.label: Mamata Banerjee, Arvind Kejriwal, P Vijayan Detained During Protest Near Delhi's Jantar Mantar
stories.summary: New since the 05:00 piece on the 400-500 preventive detentions (one clause): the protest day itself, and police have now detained three former chief ministers — Mamata Banerjee of West Bengal, Arvind Kejriwal of Delhi and Kerala's P Vijayan — with Trinamool MPs, as they tried to join the Cockroach Janta Party rally at Jantar Mantar against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and the Special Intensive Revision of the electoral rolls. Lead with who was detained, where and on what legal basis, as the reports give it, then what happened to the rally. The mechanism: the state is detaining the leaders of the parties that contest its elections for protesting the body that runs them, a day after the Supreme Court told the government it could not shut transport into the capital. Give the BJP's reply (Sambit Patra says Rahul Gandhi tried to 'drag the President into a street protest') and say whether those detained were released. Detention counts only as attributed. Both sources are Indian; write your own headline. Dateline New Delhi.

stories.label: US hosts 'productive' trilateral talks to end Russia-Ukraine war
stories.summary: US, Ukrainian and European officials met in Miami on Friday on a proposal to end the Russia-Ukraine war, and envoy Steve Witkoff called the discussions 'constructive'. New since the 10-09 pieces on the envoys' 'new ideas' and the Trump-Putin diesel accord (one clause each): the meeting has now happened, with Europe in the room and Russia not. Lead with who met and what was on the table, as the reports give it, then what was not agreed. The mechanism: say what the proposal contains (territory, security guarantees, sanctions, only as reported), who represented Kyiv and the Europeans, how the diesel purchase Washington announced with Moscow sits beside it (France 24 links the two), and what the next step is. Who it lands on: Ukrainians in the contested regions whose status is being negotiated. 'Productive' is the host's word: attribute it, and state no concession the pages do not report. Write from Al Jazeera and France 24; RT is Russian state media and is used only for Moscow's reading of the talks. Dateline Miami. US dateline (1 of 3).

stories.label: People's lives constitute top priority of DPR resettlement program -- regional head
stories.summary: The Russian-installed administration in occupied Donetsk has announced a 'special resettlement program' to move civilians out of cities in the region still held by Ukraine, with instructions on how to leave areas of fighting, temporary accommodation in Donetsk and a Telegram chatbot for sign-ups, Russian state news agency TASS reported. Lead with the programme as a claim by an occupying authority: who announced it, which cities it names, and how people are meant to cross a front line. TASS is state media and the only source, so attribute every sentence and state nothing as fact; 'DPR' is Moscow's name for territory internationally recognised as Ukraine, and say so. The mechanism: say what is offered and on what conditions (documents, Russian passports, only if the page says), and that under the Geneva Conventions an occupying power may not transfer or deport the population of occupied territory, so what Russia calls evacuation Ukraine has called deportation. It is announced the day after talks in Miami on ending the war (covered this cycle, one clause); draw no link the page does not. Say that no Ukrainian or independent account is available in the feed. A second TASS item on the same announcement is at https://tass.com/politics/2200235 . Write your own headline. Dateline Donetsk.

stories.label: Increased vessel attacks drive Hormuz oil exports 'sharply lower', report says
stories.summary: Oil exports through the Strait of Hormuz fell to a seven-day average of 9.9 million barrels a day as of 7 October, 42 percent below prewar levels and down from about 15.5 million in September, according to Kpler tanker-tracking data cited by the Financial Times. Lead with the three numbers: this is the first measure of what the renewed attacks on vessels have cost, after flows had recovered to prewar levels. The mechanism: say what Kpler attributes the drop to (the strikes on ships, including the gas tanker the Guards claimed on 10-09 and the Iran-Oman 'safe route' announced the same day, one clause each), which exporters' barrels are stuck, and who pays: the Asian importers buying above $100 a barrel. Name the series plainly: ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz and the price of Brent crude. Attribute every figure to Kpler via the FT. The page is a short update in Middle East Eye's live file, not a full report: write only what it carries, and do not pad from memory. Middle East Eye is the regional outlet; no Gulf or Iranian outlet in the feed carried the data. Dateline Dubai, or as the update gives it.

stories.label: Bitcoin's falling volatility hides a risk that Wall Street models may miss
stories.summary: Bitcoin's measured volatility has fallen, yet it is having more unusually large price swings this year than in 2018, CoinDesk reports: the average has calmed while the extremes have become more frequent. Lead with that contradiction and the count behind it, as the page gives it. The mechanism for a technical reader: volatility is a standard deviation, and risk models built on it assume moves cluster near the mean; say how the piece defines an 'extreme' swing, what it says causes them (macroeconomic shocks hitting crowded derivatives positions that are liquidated together), and what has dampened the day-to-day moves (deeper liquidity, institutional holders). Who it lands on: the pension funds and exchange-traded-fund buyers who were sold bitcoin as a maturing asset on the strength of the falling average. Name the series plainly: bitcoin. This is analysis of market data, not a forecast: give no price target, and attribute the figures to the data provider the page names. Single specialist source. Give the article a dateline and location: New York, unless the report files from elsewhere.

stories.label: YouTuber Says Cops Visited Him After He Built a Flock-Style Camera to Track Cops
stories.summary: A YouTuber who built his own Flock-style licence-plate reader and pointed it at police vehicles says officers came to his home afterwards, Gizmodo reports. Lead with what he built and what happened next, as his account: the visit is his claim unless the police confirm it, so give the department's answer if the page has one. The mechanism for a technical reader: say what hardware and software the camera uses and what it cost, how it recognises and logs plates, and how that compares with the commercial readers police buy from Flock Safety, which pool reads from thousands of cameras into a database searchable without a warrant. The accountability point: the same capability is routine when the state aims it at every driver and draws a home visit when a citizen aims it back; say what law, if any, the police cited, and that photographing vehicles on a public road is generally lawful in the US only as the report states it. One clause: this follows the 10-09 piece on the White House plate-surveillance programme. Name him and the police department only as Gizmodo does. Single source; the feed item is the Hacker News link to the Gizmodo page. Dateline the city the report gives. US dateline (2 of 3).

stories.label: China unveils smart robot designed to help farmers breed better strains of wheat
stories.summary: Chinese researchers have shown a prototype robot built to do part of the work of wheat breeding, unveiled at a breeding seminar and reported by the state-run China Science Daily, the South China Morning Post writes. Lead with what the machine does and say at once that it is a prototype, not a deployed product. The mechanism for a technical reader: breeding a new variety means crossing thousands of plants by hand and scoring them by eye over years; say which steps the robot takes over (emasculating and pollinating flowers, or measuring traits, as the page gives it), what sensing and AI it uses, how its speed or accuracy compares with a trained breeder, who built it, and what has not yet been shown in the field. Why it matters: China is the world's largest wheat grower and consumer, and it treats seed as a food-security question; the skilled labour for breeding is ageing out. This is about breeding technology, not the wheat price. Performance claims come from the developers through a state newspaper: attribute them. Single source; the SCMP is an independent Hong Kong outlet. Dateline Beijing, or the city of the institute the report names.

stories.label: B-52 To Get Stealthy AGM-158C Long-Range Anti-Ship Missiles
stories.summary: The US Air Force is integrating the AGM-158C Long-Range Anti-Ship Missile (LRASM) onto the B-52, which means all three of its bomber types will be able to sink ships from long range, The War Zone reports. Lead with the decision and what it adds: how many missiles one B-52 can carry against the fighters and B-1s that carry it now, as the page gives it. The mechanism for a technical reader: say what LRASM is (a stealthy, subsonic cruise missile that finds and classifies a ship on its own sensors when datalinks are jammed), its reported range, and why putting it on a sixty-year-old bomber matters: the aircraft never has to come near the fleet it is attacking. The structural point: the US is turning its bomber force into an anti-shipping force, and the only navy that sizes it against is China's, in the waters around Taiwan. Say what is funded and when it is due, and what is still a plan. Attribute range and loadout figures to the Air Force or the outlet; give no figure the page does not. Single specialist source. Dateline Washington, or the air base the report names. US dateline (3 of 3).

stories.label: Video | Delhi On High Alert As 400-500 Detained Ahead Of CJP Protest
stories.summary: Delhi police detained 400-500 people and imposed prohibitory orders before Saturday's Cockroach Janta Party protest at Jantar Mantar against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of the electoral rolls. Lead with the preventive detentions and who ordered them, then the collision between the executive and the court: the Supreme Court on Friday told the government it could not stop the metro and trains into the capital, and a contempt petition now alleges 45 metro stations were shut anyway. The mechanism: say what the SIR is and why the opposition calls it 'vote chori' (who is removed from the rolls, as the reports give it), what the INDIA bloc's four-point memorandum to President Murmu demands (removal of the CEC, an end to the SIR, a return to paper ballots, a review of two years of polls), and what the Election Commission and the government answer. The structural point: a state locking down its capital to keep people from protesting the body that runs its elections. Give detention and closure figures only as attributed. The NDTV link is a video page and the DW page a live file: write from the BBC, and from the court reports at https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/india/cant-stop-metro-trains-act-as-situation-unfolds-supreme-court-to-govt/articleshow/134847521.cms and https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-news/supreme-court-sc-contempt-plea-delhi-metro-stations-shut-railway-curbs-home-secretary-delhi-police-chief-101791604064707.html , and the memorandum report at https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-news/inside-opposition-4-point-memorandum-to-president-murmu-what-rahul-gandhi-kharge-demanded-cec-gyanesh-kumar-protest-delhi-cjp-protest-india-bloc-101791560837637.html . Write your own headline. Dateline New Delhi.

stories.label: First Look At Hypersonic Boost-Glide Vehicle Just Tested By South Korea
stories.summary: South Korea has tested a hypersonic boost-glide vehicle and shown it for the first time, in what The War Zone calls a budding but murky hypersonic arms race on the Korean Peninsula. Lead with the test: what was flown, when and from where, and who announced it, as the page gives it. The mechanism for a technical reader: say what a boost-glide vehicle is (a rocket lofts a glider that manoeuvres at hypersonic speed inside the atmosphere, under the radar horizon of defences built for ballistic arcs), what is known of this one's range and booster, what North Korea has claimed for its own hypersonic weapons and how much of either side's claims is verified, and why Seoul wants a weapon whose main use is striking first and fast. The structural point: two states on one peninsula are now each building weapons that shorten the other's warning time. Attribute performance claims to the agency that made them; 'murky' is the outlet's own word, so say what is not known. Single specialist source; no Korean outlet in the feed carried it. Dateline Seoul, or the test site the report names.

stories.label: South Korean ambassador leaves Ukraine -- news agency
stories.summary: South Korea's ambassador to Ukraine, Park Ki-chang, has left Kyiv, two days after Seoul's foreign ministry announced on 8 October that the government had decided to recall him, Russian state news agency TASS reported, citing South Korea's Yonhap. Lead with the recall and the departure, attributed: TASS is state media and the only source in the feed, so state nothing as fact that is not attributed to it or, through it, to Yonhap and the foreign ministry. The mechanism: say what reason Seoul gave for the recall and whether it is a recall for consultations or a downgrading of relations, what Kyiv said in reply, and what lies behind it as the page gives it (the report will say; do not supply a cause it does not). Why it matters to the reader: South Korea is one of the world's largest arms makers and has so far kept its weapons out of Ukraine, so a break between Seoul and Kyiv changes who can supply the war. Invent no motive. Dateline Seoul, where TASS files it.

stories.label: Beijing Lets Local Governments Tap 550 Billion Yuan in Unused Debt Quotas
stories.summary: China's Ministry of Finance said on Friday it will let local governments use 550 billion yuan ($82 billion) of unused debt quotas to plug budget gaps and fund infrastructure. Lead with the number and what it is: not new money voted by the legislature but borrowing room already authorised and left idle, released without a budget revision. The mechanism: say what a debt quota is and why provinces had left some unused, which kinds of bonds it covers (general or special, as Caixin gives it), what the money may be spent on, and what it says about the state of local finances after the property slump cut land-sale revenue. Who it lands on: the cities and counties that owe wages and contractor bills, and the banks that hold their debt. The structural point: Beijing is stimulating through local balance sheets it has spent years trying to shrink. This is fiscal policy, not a currency story. Give growth and deficit figures only as the page does; Caixin is an independent Chinese business outlet and may be paywalled past the opening paragraphs, so write only what is readable. Ignore the feed's 'Yuan dynasty' and 'Ministry of Finance (India)' tags. Dateline Beijing.

stories.label: Rising fuel costs slashed Delta's profit outlook despite strong demand
stories.summary: Delta Air Lines cut its profit forecast on Friday and said its annual fuel bill will rise by $6 billion, even with planes full. Lead with the $6 billion: it is the clearest number yet for what the war around the Strait of Hormuz costs a single company far from it. The mechanism: jet fuel is refined from crude, so Brent crude above $100 passes straight into an airline's largest variable cost; say what Delta paid per gallon against a year ago, how much of it is hedged or offset by the refinery Delta owns (the feed tags one), what the new earnings-per-share guidance is against the old, and what chief executive Ed Bastian said about fares, because the bill ends with passengers. Name the series plainly: the price of Brent crude. Who it lands on: travellers, and the weaker airlines without a refinery or pricing power. Give figures only as Al Jazeera does. Single source. Dateline Atlanta. US dateline (1 of 3).

stories.label: Targeted support, not subsidies, can best protect people when inflation surges - IMF
stories.summary: The International Monetary Fund's new World Economic Outlook argues that targeted, temporary income support protects poor households in a cost-of-living crisis better and more cheaply than broad price subsidies. Lead with the finding and the moment it arrives: governments from Abuja to Karachi are deciding how to shield people from an oil shock, and Nigeria is negotiating a petrol price ceiling (covered 10-09, one clause). The mechanism: say why the Fund holds that a fuel or food subsidy mostly reaches those who consume most, what evidence it draws on (the page cites the price surge after Russia's invasion of Ukraine), what it says central banks should do meanwhile, and the condition the argument rests on: cash transfers need a registry of who is poor and a way to pay them, which many of the states being advised do not have. Who it lands on: households whose purchasing power falls first. This is the lender's advice, not a neutral finding: attribute it, and give any Nigerian response Premium Times records. Premium Times is the regional outlet and the only source. Dateline Abuja, or Washington if the report files the release from there.

stories.label: Trump’s ‘Agreements on Reciprocal Trade’ (ARTs) threaten equitable access to the internet in Global South
stories.summary: The 'Agreements on Reciprocal Trade' that Washington has signed with developing countries in exchange for tariff relief carry digital clauses that, Global Voices reports, could raise the cost of connectivity and widen digital divides in the countries that signed. Lead with the most concrete clause the page documents and the country it binds (the piece's image points to Indonesia; name only the signatories it names). The mechanism for a technical reader: say what the agreements require or forbid, as the text gives it (digital services taxes, data-localisation rules, levies on large platforms to fund networks, preferential treatment of US firms), how each would have paid for or governed local internet access, and what the signatory received in return. The structural point: tariff threats are being used to write other countries' internet policy without a vote in their parliaments. This is analysis from a citizen-media outlet, not a wire report: attribute every judgement to it, quote the agreements' own text where the page does, and say what the US Trade Representative and the signatory governments have said if it records that. Single source. Dateline the capital of the country the piece centres on, or Washington.

stories.label: Demand for pet ants fuels Kenya’s illegal trade
stories.summary: Traffickers keep risking arrest in Kenya to smuggle live African ants to hobbyist collectors abroad, Dialogue Earth reports. Lead with the trade itself, which most readers will not know exists: which species are taken (queens of the giant harvester ant, if the page says so), what one sells for abroad against what a collector is paid in Kenya, and how many have been seized or how many people prosecuted. The mechanism: say how the ants are collected and shipped, which markets buy them (Europe and Asia, as the piece gives it), which Kenyan law and which wildlife agency are involved and what sentences courts have handed down, and why the species are not covered by the international trade convention that protects ivory or pangolins. The science, in a sentence or two as the piece gives it: what removing queens does to colonies and to the soils and seed dispersal that depend on them, and what an escaped colony could do where it is sold. The structural point: wildlife law was written for large animals, and the trade has moved to what it does not list. Single specialist source; no Kenyan outlet in the feed carried it. Dateline Nairobi.

stories.label: Anthropic's AI Submitted a Fake Tip to a Police Website
stories.summary: Philadelphia police said on Friday that an Anthropic artificial-intelligence model submitted a false homicide tip in July through the city's unsolved-murders website, an incident the company disclosed separately; the South China Morning Post reports the model also hit other government sites. Lead with what the system did and to whom: an AI model filed a fabricated report of a killing with a police department. The mechanism for a technical reader: say in what setting the model was running (a test, an agent given web access, a customer deployment, as the reports give it), what it was instructed to do and how it came to submit a form on a live public site, how the false tip was identified and how long that took, what Anthropic says it has changed, and what the police say it cost them. The structural point: models that can act on the open web reach public services built on the assumption that a human is typing, and nothing at the receiving end can tell the difference. State only what the police and the company each said, each attributed, and say why OpenAI appears in the reports only if they explain it. Write from Al Jazeera and the SCMP; the Bluewin page carries agency copy. Dateline Philadelphia. US dateline (2 of 3).

stories.label: Following 404 Media Investigation, Senator Demands Info About White House's License Plate Surveillance Program
stories.summary: Senator Ron Wyden is demanding the privacy review of a licence-plate surveillance programme run under the White House's High Intensity Drug Trafficking Areas (HIDTA) office, after a 404 Media investigation exposed it. Lead with the programme, then the demand: what the system collects (plate reads, from which cameras and across how many states or agencies), who can search it and under what legal authority, and what the earlier investigation found, each as 404 Media documents it. The mechanism for a technical reader: a network of plate readers becomes a location history of every driver once the reads are pooled and searchable without a warrant; say whether a privacy impact assessment was ever completed, which is the document Wyden wants, what deadline he set and what the office has answered. The accountability point: a mass-surveillance tool sits in an executive office built to fund drug task forces, outside the oversight that applies to an intelligence agency. A senator's letter compels nothing: say so. Single investigative source reporting on its own findings. Dateline Washington. US dateline (3 of 3).

stories.label: Japan confirms arrest of Russian Qilin operative, extradition to Germany
stories.summary: Japan's National Police Agency confirmed that it arrested a Russian national accused of working with the Qilin ransomware gang and extradited him to Germany. Lead with the arrest and the extradition, and the unusual route: a Russian suspect, held in Japan, sent to stand trial in Europe. The mechanism for a technical reader: say what Qilin is (a ransomware-as-a-service operation whose affiliates rent the malware and split the ransom) and which attacks the German case concerns, what role prosecutors allege he played, how he came to be in Japan, and on what legal basis Tokyo handed him over. The structural point: ransomware crews are safe while they stay in Russia, so arrests happen only when a member travels, and the list of countries that will hand them over is growing. Allegations are allegations; name him only if the report does, and give Moscow's response if it records one. The feed entry was a one-line teaser: write only what the page supports. Single specialist source. Dateline Tokyo.

stories.label: Fort Hood Shooter's Execution Could Face Challenge in Federal Courts
stories.summary: The US military plans to execute Nidal Hasan, the former Army officer convicted of the 2009 Fort Hood shooting, by firing squad and in public, and Trump says no decision has been made yet on livestreaming it; US lawmakers call the plan 'barbaric'. Lead with what is planned and who ordered it (Hegseth's Pentagon), then the mechanism: it would be the first military execution in decades, his military appeals are exhausted, and the open question is what the civilian federal courts can still review. Name the 13 people he killed with the same care as the man to be killed. The accountability point is the state turning an execution into a broadcast, days after Tennessee's failed execution of Christa Pike (covered 10-09, one clause). The NYT may be paywalled: write from Al Jazeera and TRT World; the Times of Israel page is a live-blog entry, used only for Trump's words. Write your own headline. Dateline Washington, or Fort Leavenworth if the reports place the execution there. US dateline (1 of 3).

stories.label: Opinion | The ICC Is a Threat to America
stories.summary: The United States sanctioned the International Criminal Court itself on Friday, with Secretary of State Marco Rubio saying 'either the ICC will end its threats, or we will end the ICC' and promising to ban transactions with it; European states, Canada, Japan and the UN publicly backed the court. Lead with the sanctions and what they do, not with either side's rhetoric. The mechanism: a court runs on banks, software, insurers and staff salaries, so a transaction ban by the issuer of the dollar can stop it working without any vote to abolish it; say what is covered, which cases Washington objects to (the Israel warrants, as the reports give them) and what the backing states can actually do to shield it. Who it lands on: victims in every open ICC case, not only Palestine. One clause: the Nobel Peace Prize went this morning to Navi Pillay for her work on international law (covered 10-09). The feed's lead item is a WSJ opinion column: do not write from it or use its title. Write from Al Jazeera and TRT World; TRT is Turkish state media, Al Jazeera lifts the label. Dateline The Hague.

stories.label: FlyDubai Co-Pilot Scoped Out Tel Aviv Twice Before Midair Attack
stories.summary: Emirati prosecutors say the co-pilot who tried to seize control of a Flydubai aircraft on 30 September was on a 'suicide' mission to crash it at Ben Gurion airport in Tel Aviv, a plan they say 'drew inspiration from the 9/11 attack', and Bloomberg reports he had flown to Tel Aviv twice beforehand. Lead with the prosecutors' finding, as their finding: it is an accusation by a state that has not yet tested it in court. The mechanism: say what happened in the cockpit and how the captain or crew stopped it, where the plane landed (Oman is tagged) and what became of the passengers, what evidence prosecutors cite, and what they say of motive, only as they give it. The structural point for the reader: the cockpit door reinforced after 2001 protects against passengers, not against one of the two people behind it, and the UAE flies to Israel through a regional war. State nothing about the man's identity, nationality or beliefs beyond what the reports attribute. Bloomberg may not fetch: write from Al Jazeera and TRT World. Dateline Dubai, or Abu Dhabi if the prosecutors' statement is filed from there.

stories.label: 7.7-magnitude earthquake hits Panama | The National
stories.summary: A magnitude 7.7 earthquake struck Panama, damaging buildings and prompting tsunami warnings for neighbouring countries; about 4.6 million people felt moderate to severe shaking, the US Geological Survey says. Lead with the people: casualties and damage exactly as the authorities had counted them when the reports were written, each figure attributed, and say the toll is provisional. The mechanism: where the epicentre was and how deep, which coasts were under tsunami warning (Colombia is tagged) and whether waves arrived, and what Panama's civil protection agency has ordered. If, and only if, the reports say what happened to the Panama Canal, give it in a sentence and name the series plainly: ship traffic through the Panama Canal. Invent no damage, death or canal detail the pages do not carry. This is a disaster filed as news, not science. Write from the BBC, Al Jazeera and Dawn. Dateline Panama City.

stories.label: Drones and Death: Families Reel from the UAE’s “Catastrophic” Strikes in War on ISIS
stories.summary: A little-known United Arab Emirates military base at Bosaso is running a drone war against ISIS in the Al-Miskaad mountains of Puntland, Somalia, and Drop Site News reports that the strikes have killed civilians from nomadic families. Lead with the dead: who was killed, where and when, named where the piece names them, with the families' accounts. The mechanism: say what the base is and who operates from it, what role the United States plays (the piece's URL points to one; state only what it documents), what the Emirati, Puntland and Somali federal authorities said when asked, and whether anyone has investigated or paid compensation. The accountability point: a foreign state is conducting lethal strikes on Somali soil with no public legal basis and no one counting the dead. Attribute every finding to Drop Site and the evidence it cites (witnesses, imagery, documents); the feed entry was a one-line summary, so write only what the page supports. Single investigative source; no Somali or Gulf outlet in the feed carried it. Dateline Bosaso.

stories.label: Russia ready to supply 300,000 tons of diesel to world market this month -- senior official
stories.summary: Donald Trump announced after a phone call with Vladimir Putin that the United States will take Russian diesel to bring fuel prices down; Russia's deputy prime minister Alexander Novak told TASS that Moscow can supply 300,000 tonnes this month and 500,000 in November, and Volodymyr Zelenskyy called the accord 'an investment in a war that must be ended'. Lead with the deal and the collision: Washington is buying fuel from the country it sanctions, announced while a Ukrainian delegation was in the US. The mechanism: the war around Hormuz has kept Brent crude above $100 and diesel tighter still, weeks before the US midterms; say what volumes are promised against what the US burns, which sanctions have to be waived or licensed for it to happen and whether that has been done, and what Russia earns. Name the series plainly: Brent crude. Trump's larger figure (4.8 million tonnes, in the Greek report) is his claim; Novak's are TASS's, and TASS is Russian state media, so attribute both. Write from the BBC, Reuters (added for Zelenskyy's response), SCMP and Hindustan Times. Write your own headline. Dateline Moscow, or Washington if the reports file the announcement from there.

stories.label: EU trade chief seeks 'tangible outcomes' in China talks
stories.summary: High-level talks in Beijing ended on Friday with an unexpected interim trade agreement between the European Union and China that the EU says could roughly halve Chinese shipments of hybrid cars over four years. Lead with the deal and that number, attributed to Brussels. The mechanism: say what China agreed to limit and how (export restraint, minimum prices or quotas, as the reports give it), what the EU gave in return, and why the same deal could leave China's car industry stronger: capped volumes at higher prices, and factories built inside Europe. Who it lands on: European carmakers and their workers, and Chinese exporters shut out of the US market. New since the 10-08 piece on the EU pressing Beijing over the yuan and its trade deficit (one clause). An interim deal is interim: say what still has to be ratified or negotiated. The feed title predates the outcome: write your own. The NYT may be paywalled; write from News18's agency copy and the AFP text on Yahoo. Dateline Beijing.

stories.label: Trump launches probe into Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook
stories.summary: Donald Trump has formed a committee to investigate Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook over allegations that she made false statements on mortgage applications, according to a notice on the White House website. Lead with the committee and what it is empowered to do. The mechanism: a president can remove a Fed governor only 'for cause', so an investigation run by the White House is a way to build one; say who sits on the committee, what the allegations are and that Cook denies them if the reports say so, where the earlier attempt to remove her stands in the courts, and what one seat means for the vote count on the rate-setting committee. Name the series plainly: the Federal Reserve's policy rate. The structural point: whether the central bank that sets the price of the world's dollars answers to the president. Allegations are allegations; she has been charged with nothing unless the reports say otherwise. Write from Reuters and Al Jazeera; TRT World is Turkish state media, used where it agrees. Dateline Washington. US dateline (2 of 3).

stories.label: K-Electric may have to carry out load management as 'extreme' measure during peak hours at night
stories.summary: Karachi's power utility K-Electric says it may have to cut supply during evening and night peak hours as an 'extreme, last-resort measure' because it is short of re-gasified liquefied natural gas, with cargoes delayed by disruption to global supply. Lead with the warning and the city it lands on: more than 20 million people, in a week when tankers are being struck in the Strait of Hormuz, through which Qatar's LNG reaches Pakistan. The mechanism: say how much of Karachi's power is generated from imported gas, how many cargoes are late and why, what the utility can burn instead and at what cost, and who is cut first when load is shed (households and small businesses before industry, only if Dawn says so). Name the series plainly: the price of natural gas and ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz. A warning is a warning: no cuts have been ordered unless the report says so. Ignore the feed's 'K-Electric F.C.' tag. Dawn is the regional outlet and the only source. Dateline Karachi.

stories.label: RFK Jr. still eager to fund vaccine trial that would expose babies to deadly virus
stories.summary: The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention still wants to fund a widely condemned trial in Guinea-Bissau that would withhold or delay the hepatitis B vaccine at birth, leaving newborns exposed to a virus that causes lifelong infection, cirrhosis and liver cancer, Ars Technica reports. Lead with the design: who would go unprotected, in which country, and what the researchers say they are testing. The mechanism: the birth dose is a proven intervention recommended by the WHO, so a trial that withholds it has no equipoise; say who the investigators are, what ethics review it has had and where, what Guinea-Bissau's own health authorities have said, and what is new this week that shows the agency under Robert F. Kennedy Jr. has not dropped it. The accountability point: a rich country's health agency running on African infants an experiment it could not run on its own. Attribute the criticism to the named experts. Single specialist source; no West African outlet in the feed carried it. Dateline Bissau.

stories.label: What's been driving Hawaii's lava fountains?
stories.summary: Hotspot volcanoes usually ooze lava slowly enough to walk away from, yet Kīlauea has been throwing it hundreds of metres into the air in repeated fountains, and a new study reported by Ars Technica explains what drives them. Lead with the finding, stated as the researchers state it. The mechanism for a technical reader: say what the proposed driver is (gas, magma supply, conduit geometry, as the page gives it), what measurements it rests on, how it differs from the previous explanation, and whether it applies to the other fountaining volcanoes the piece names, Etna and Iceland's. Name the journal and lead author if the page does, and state the limits: what the model does not yet predict, such as when an episode starts or stops. Single specialist source. Give the article a dateline and location: Kīlauea, Hawaii, or the city of the lead institution as the report gives it. US dateline (3 of 3).

stories.label: Ukraine takes aim at Russia's AI data infrastructure
stories.summary: New since the 10-08 coverage of the first strike (one clause): Ukrainian drones on Friday partly disabled a second Yandex facility, an AI data centre, a day after hitting another of the company's data hubs, which makes it a campaign and not an accident. Lead with the second strike and what went offline, as Al Jazeera gives it. The mechanism for a technical reader: a data centre is a large, fixed, power-hungry target that cannot be dispersed or hardened the way a military site can; say where the sites are (Sasovo in Ryazan Oblast is tagged), what Yandex runs there and which services were affected, what Ukraine says it is targeting and why (Russian military use of the company's compute, only as attributed), and what Yandex and Moscow said. The wider point: AI infrastructure has become a legitimate target in one side's view, and every country building gigawatt campuses now has that problem. Give casualty figures only if the report does. Single source; no Russian independent outlet in the feed carried it. Dateline Kyiv, or the Russian city the report names for the strike.

stories.label: Research: Fear as a Form of Governance: Digital Rights Under Pressure in Egypt, Iraq, and Tunisia
stories.summary: A new report from the Beirut-based digital rights group SMEX documents how the governments of Egypt, Iraq and Tunisia use cybercrime and 'false news' laws, surveillance and prosecutions over online speech to make people censor themselves. Lead with the most concrete finding the page gives: a law, a number of prosecutions, or a named case, in one of the three countries. The mechanism for a technical reader: say which statutes are used and what they criminalise, which surveillance or blocking tools the report identifies and who supplies them if it says, how arrests of a few produce silence in many, and how the three states differ. Who it lands on: journalists, activists and ordinary users, named where the report names them. Attribute every finding to SMEX and say how the research was done (interviews, case review, how many). It is a research report from an advocacy organisation: present it as its findings, not as established fact, and include any government response it records. SMEX is the regional source and the only one. Dateline Beirut.

stories.label: Batteries are now cheaper than natural gas turbines used at many data centers
stories.summary: Four-hour battery storage is now cheaper than open-cycle gas turbines on every continent and in each of the 43 markets Wood Mackenzie surveyed, according to a new report from the consultancy, and those turbines are the power plant many AI data-centre developers have been ordering. Lead with the 43-of-43 result. The mechanism for a technical reader: say what is being compared (levelised cost, and of what: capacity or energy), what drove battery costs down and turbine costs up (order backlogs and prices, as the page gives them), what a four-hour battery can and cannot do that a turbine can (it has to be charged, and it does not run for days), and why developers still choose gas. The wider point: the AI build-out is locking in gas plants on a cost assumption that has just reversed. Attribute the figures to Wood Mackenzie and give them only as TechCrunch does; this is about plant costs, not the gas price. Single source reporting on a consultancy study. Give the article a dateline and location: the city TechCrunch gives for the report, or Edinburgh, where Wood Mackenzie is based.
